COMET THROUGH THE SLIT — a bright comet trails its long dust-tail across the cold slice of dome-framed night, sharp stars scattered around it.
GREAT FULL MOON — the great full moon hangs perfectly centred in the dome opening, its cratered face brilliant and cold against pure black.
GREEN AURORA RIPPLING — green aurora ripples in slow curtains above the open terrace, the bright constellations burning steady behind its cold fire.
MILKY WAY BAND — the dense milky band of the galaxy spills across the dome slit, ten thousand stars packed into that cold river of light.
CRESCENT AND PLANET — a thin crescent moon and one brilliant planet hang low together in the cold western dark framed by the terrace rail.
METEOR STREAK — a bright meteor burns a sharp white line across the dome gap, gone in an instant, leaving cold black sky behind.
TOTAL ECLIPSE CORONA — the dark disc of totality floats in the dome opening, its white corona peeling outward in cold streamers against black sky.
SHARP WINTER CONSTELLATIONS — the winter constellations blaze sharp and hard in a clear cold black sky seen cleanly through the wide dome slit.
STORM-CLOUDS PARTING — heavy clouds tear open revealing a bright field of stars beyond, cold and sharp, the dome slit framing that sudden gap.
PERSEID SHOWER — three meteors at once rake bright lines across the dome opening, the summer sky cold at altitude and dense with background stars.
SATURN LOW AND STEADY — one steady cream-coloured point burns low in the cold sky above the terrace, distinct and unwavering where all other stars scintillate.
JUPITER RISING — a brilliant cream point climbs slowly through the dome slit, brighter than any star, the cold sky sharp and black around it.
DOUBLE-STAR FIELD — the eyepiece field swarms with paired stars of contrasting colour, gold and blue, packed tight in cold black sky.
SCORPIUS RISING — the great scorpion constellation clears the roofline and hangs in the dome slit, its red heart-star burning in the cold southern sky.
ORION IN WINTER — Orion strides perfectly centred in the dome opening, his belt and sword brilliant, cold blue-white stars sharp against pure black.
AURORA VIOLET CROWN — violet and pale green aurora forms a crown above the terrace observatory, the pole-star burning steady through its cold shifting curtain.
GEGENSCHEIN FAINT — a faint oval glow of gegenschein floats opposite the sun in cold dark sky above the dome, barely brighter than the stars around it.
MARS AT OPPOSITION — a fierce blood-orange point burns through the dome slit at opposition, steadier and ruddier than anything else in the cold black sky.
PLEIADES CLUSTER — the tight blue cluster of the Pleiades hangs in the dome gap, seven cold points distinct to the eye above the instrument.
COMET NUCLEUS CLOSE — the comet's bright condensed nucleus glows at dome-slit centre, its curved dust tail sweeping away into cold black star-scattered sky.
HAZY ANDROMEDA PATCH — a faint oval smear of light floats above the terrace among hard cold stars, no planet, no comet, only that distant soft glow.
ECLIPSED MOON RED — the totally eclipsed moon hangs blood-red and strange in the dome opening, stars now visible around it in the cold darkened sky.
CLEARING AFTER RAIN — the last cloud-rack peels back across the dome slit and cold washed stars emerge, sharp and thick after the night's rain.
WINTER SOLSTICE SKY — the long solstice night pours cold and clear through the dome, Gemini and Auriga blazing high, the galaxy faint below them.
ZODIACAL LIGHT — a faint pyramid of cold light leans up from the western horizon through the dome slit, tracing the plane of the solar system.
FRAMED FULL MOON — a great full moon hangs perfectly in the dome opening, its cratered face brilliant against the black, cold light flooding the instrument below.
AURORA OVER THE TERRACE — green-and-violet aurora ripples across the vast cold star-field above the rooftop array, the sharp constellations burning bright behind the shifting curtains.
CONSTELLATION FIELD — sharp familiar constellations stand perfectly defined in a clear cold black sky seen through the dome, each star a hard bright point.
STORM PARTING — heavy clouds split apart to reveal a sudden deep corridor of cold stars blazing through the gap above the terrace telescope.
SATURN LOW — Saturn hangs cold and steady low in the dome gap, its ring-plane tilted faintly visible even to the naked eye in clear black air.
WINTER ORION — Orion stands tall and brilliant through the dome slit, Rigel and Betelgeuse burning cold blue and amber against the hard black night.
DOUBLE STAR — two close bright stars glow through the slit, one warm gold and one ice-blue, a cold binary jewel sharp in the dark.
AURORAL PILLAR — a single tall green pillar of aurora rises straight above the terrace parapet into the cold star-scattered sky, trembling slowly at its crest.
EARTHSHINE CRESCENT — a slender crescent moon glows in the dome opening, its dark face softly lit by earthshine, cold and ghostly against surrounding stars.
BLOOD MOON RISING — the fully eclipsed moon rises deep copper-red through the dome slit, enormous and dim, the stars around it unusually bright and cold.
COMET NUCLEUS — a great comet hangs almost motionless through the dome gap, its bright head vivid, its tail sweeping cold across a quarter of the sky.
JUPITER AND MOONS — Jupiter burns steady and brilliant low in the dome slit, its four small moons faintly visible strung cold on either side.
CLEAR ZENITH — the zenith framed by the open dome is a perfect cold black circle packed with stars, the Milky Way cutting straight across it.
NORTHERN LIGHTS SURGE — aurora suddenly surges brilliant green overhead across the full open terrace, the constellations dimming behind the cold rippling luminous curtain.
SUMMER TRIANGLE — the bright Summer Triangle fills the upper dome slit, Vega, Deneb, and Altair cold and unwavering in the clear black summer night.
CLOUDS BREAKING — ragged storm-clouds peel back above the terrace to expose a raw cold patch of stars blazing hard and clear in the gap.
LEONID STORM — Leonid meteors rain in dozens through the dome slit, the cold radiant point in Leo spilling bright trails across the entire black field.
MILKY WAY OVERHEAD — the dense galactic band arches through the dome slit, ten thousand cold stars packed into a luminous river across black sky.
CRESCENT AND BRIGHT PLANET — a thin crescent moon and blazing Venus hang low together in the dome gap, pale twilight still fading at the horizon edge.
JUPITER NEAR OPPOSITION — Jupiter blazes low and steady through the dome gap, its pale disc enormous this night, four moons faintly bracketing it.
FAINT ZODIACAL LIGHT — a ghostly pyramid of reflected dust-light rises from the horizon through the slit, the ecliptic faintly glowing between scattered stars.
DOUBLE STAR PAIR — two close stars burn side by side through the dome slit, one gold, one pale blue, steady cold points against the black.
SATURN RISING — Saturn clears the roofline and enters the dome slit, its rings tilted and sharp-edged, a cold steady jewel against the star-field.
RED MARS AT OPPOSITION — Mars burns an unwavering blood-red through the dome gap, brighter than any nearby star, the open sky cold and absolutely clear.
AURORA WITH STARS BEHIND — a violet aurora sheet brightens over the terrace without drowning the background stars, Ursa Major still clearly mapped through the glow.
GLOBULAR CLUSTER HIGH — the dense ancient globe of Omega Centauri glows through the dome slit, thousands of old stars compressed into one cold luminous smear.
CLOUD BREAK AT MIDNIGHT — a narrow break in heavy midnight cloud reveals one bright patch of stars through the terrace gap before closing again silently.
SECOND COMET TAIL — a diffuse secondary comet brushes the dome slit edge, its ion tail straight and blue-white, the dust tail sweeping broadly behind.
LUNAR ECLIPSE DEEP RED — the fully eclipsed moon hangs blood-copper through the dome opening, Earth's shadow complete, the surrounding stars startlingly bright and cold.
ARCTURUS AND CLEAR SKY — Arcturus blazes orange-gold and alone through the slit above the terrace, the spring sky around it coldly black and perfectly still.
AUTUMN MILKY WAY — the galaxy's dense core regions cross the dome slit diagonally, the Sagittarius star-clouds packed thick, the sky around them absolute black.
NOCTILUCENT CLOUDS — high electric-blue noctilucent clouds drift faintly above the terrace horizon while the lower sky remains black and star-filled beyond them.
SIRIUS SCINTILLATING — Sirius flashes rapidly between white and blue and red through the dome slit, atmospheric refraction splitting its fierce cold light into colour.
SHARP CONSTELLATIONS — the winter constellations stand hard and brilliant in a perfectly clear black sky, each star a cold precise point through the dome slit.
COMET TAIL FANNING — the great comet's tail fans wide across the dome slit, a pale swept arc of cold light against the deep stellar field.
GIBBOUS MOON RISING — a heavy gibbous moon clears the rooftop parapet and fills the dome gap, its mountains and mare dark against blazing cold white light.
AURORA COLUMNS — tall columns of green aurora rise straight from the horizon above the terrace rail, shimmering between the fixed cold points of the northern stars.
DENSE STAR CLUSTER — a great globular cluster hangs in the dome slit like a hazed cold jewel, surrounded by the flat black of deep night sky.
LEONID SHOWER — three meteors burn simultaneously through the dome slit, streaking from a single cold radiant point high in the dark November sky.
ECLIPSE TOTALITY — totality falls; the corona blazes in a ring above the terrace, the cold stars emerging in full daylight at the horizon beyond the dome.
ORION RISING — Orion clears the rooftop and fills the dome slit, its three belt stars aligned perfectly, Betelgeuse ruddy and cold against the winter black.
PARTING CLOUDS AND COMET — the clouds part suddenly above the terrace, and the bright comet hangs there unexpected in the cold gap, tail streaming silently east.
MILKY WAY CORE — the dense bright core of the galaxy crosses the open slit, a cold packed river of stars and dark dust-lanes in a black sky.
CRESCENT MOON SETTING — a thin crescent moon tips and sinks through the dome gap at the horizon, cold orange and fading into the last twilight band.
AURORA AND MOON — a half-moon and green aurora share the cold sky above the terrace, the aurora shifting around the steady white light of the lunar disc.
PERSEID METEOR — a brilliant Perseid flares and leaves a brief glowing train across the dome slit, the cold August stars sharp and still around its fading path.
CLOUDS BREAKING WIDE — a wide breach opens in the overcast above the terrace, and through it the Milky Way stretches cold and clear between the dark cloud-walls.
JUPITER AT OPPOSITION — a brilliant steady white planet burns in the dome slit at opposition, outshining everything around it in the cold black equatorial sky field.
TOTAL SOLAR ECLIPSE CORONA — the dark disc of the moon sits ringed by the sun's pearlescent corona, streaming in cold silence through the observatory slit above.
SATURN LOW IN THE SLIT — Saturn hangs low and steady in the brass dome opening, its rings tilted plain to the naked eye in the cold dark.
PLEIADES IN THE SLIT — the Pleiades cluster crowds the narrow dome slit, seven sisters cold and close together, the faintest members just visible in the crisp air.
DOUBLE STAR FIELD — a rich double-star field fills the dome opening, pairs of blue-white and gold burning together against the deep black beyond the brass.
WANING GIBBOUS MOON — the waning gibbous moon clears the dome slit edge, its scarred southern highlands throwing long cold shadows across the crater floors.
SOUTHERN CROSS LOW — the Southern Cross hangs very low through the terrace railing on a southern expedition night, cold and steady above the dark horizon.
SCORPIUS AND RED STAR — Scorpius curves through the dome gap, Antares burning deep amber-red at its heart against the hard cold blue of the surrounding stars.
STAR CLOUDS OF SAGITTARIUS — the rich star-clouds of Sagittarius fill the dome slit, the galactic core dense and luminous, a frosted mass in the cold black.
ANNULAR ECLIPSE RING — the annular eclipse hangs in the dome slit as a perfect ring of fierce golden sunlight encircling the black disc of the passing moon.
CASSIOPEIA AND MILKY WAY — Cassiopeia sits amid the thickest part of the Milky Way above the terrace, its W sharp, star-fields cascading behind it in cold profusion.
CLOUDS CLEARING AT ZENITH — the overcast breaks suddenly at the zenith above the dome, a ragged oval of clear black filled with brilliant stars, clouds closing again at the edges.
DAWN STAR FADE — Venus alone survives the growing blue of dawn above the terrace, brilliant and solitary as every other star drowns in the cold morning light.
MILKY WAY CROSSING THE SLIT — the dense milky band of the galaxy sweeps in a luminous river across the dome gap, ten thousand stars salted thickly through the dark.
CRESCENT MOON AND VENUS — a thin crescent moon hangs low in the dome slit, brilliant Venus burning close beside it in the cold deep blue of early night.
PERSEID SWARM — a dozen bright Perseid meteors score white lines across the dome gap in quick succession, the shower at its peak against a dense star-field.
RISING SCORPIUS — the great arc of Scorpius climbs above the terrace parapet, Antares burning red-orange at its heart, the scorpion's tail curling into the southern milky band.
LUNAR HALO — a great circular halo rings the full moon above the open terrace, ice crystals in the high cloud refracting its light into a wide pale luminous ring.
FIRST STARS AT DUSK — the dome slit opens on a deep blue twilight sky where the first stars of evening appear one by one, sharpening as the cold darkness gathers.
FOG-PARTED ZENITH — ground fog lies thick below the observatory hill but the zenith clears, and through the dome slit a perfect circle of black sky blazes with hard cold stars.
PARTING STORM-CLOUDS — storm-clouds tear apart to reveal a sudden field of cold stars through the dome slit, the edges of cloud still silver-lit.
DENSE STAR-FIELD — thousands of stars crowd the narrow strip of sky through the open dome, the faint smear of nebulae visible between bright points.
SATURN NEAR THE MERIDIAN — a steady pale golden star crosses the dome slit near meridian, Saturn unwavering where all other stars tremble slightly in cold air.
DOUBLE STARS IN THE SLIT — two close stars hang in the dome gap, a tight brilliant pair, one amber one blue-white, resolved through cold still air.
AUTUMN AURORA — a pale green aurora rises low on the northern horizon above the terrace parapet, washing the cold sky behind Cassiopeia with faint wavering light.
WINTER MILKY WAY — the winter Milky Way crosses the dome slit diagonally, Orion on one side and Gemini on the other, stars dense and cold.
PARTIAL LUNAR ECLIPSE — the earth's curved shadow bites a clean ruddy arc across the full moon hanging in the dome opening, the remainder blazing cold white.
LEONID FIREBALL — a brilliant Leonid fireball crosses the full width of the dome slit, leaving a glowing greenish train that persists several seconds among the stars.
CLOUD-BREAK AFTER RAIN — a sudden break in retreating rain-cloud reveals cold sharp stars through the dome slit, the air washed clean, every star perfectly still.
HUNTER'S MOON RISING — a great amber hunter's moon rises through thin haze above the terrace horizon, reddened by atmosphere, enormous and cold against the darkening sky.
SOUTHERN CROSS FROM THE DOME — on a southern expedition night the Southern Cross stands perfectly framed in the dome slit, four bright stars and the coal-sack dark beside them.
GEGENSCHEIN FAINT GLOW — the faint oval gegenschein glows directly opposite the sun in the midnight sky above the terrace, barely brighter than the surrounding cold star-field.
METEOR THROUGH THE GAP — a sharp bright meteor streaks across the dome slit in one cold instant, its white trail burning brief and vivid against the black.
PARTING STORM CLOUDS — heavy clouds tear apart above the terrace to reveal a cold blaze of stars, the rift widening across the dark and turbulent sky.
HARVEST FULL MOON — a vast orange full moon climbs through the dome opening, its face scarred with cold shadow-filled craters, dominating the whole night beyond the brass.
STARFIELD CORE — the galactic core hangs dense and luminous in the dome slit, a cold river of ten thousand suns packed tight against the absolute black.
VENUS AT DUSK — a razor crescent moon curves beside brilliant Venus low in the cold indigo sky, both vivid through the terrace telescope's long brass barrel.
LEONID METEOR — a blazing leonid tears a long cold scratch across the black sky visible through the dome slit, brief and violent as struck steel.
DIAMOND-RING ECLIPSE — the last bead of cold sunlight flares at the dark eclipse disc's rim, the full corona spreading wide and silent through the dome opening.
LIGHTNING AND STARS — a storm retreats beyond the terrace, lightning flickering at the horizon while overhead the cold clear sky fills with hard and brilliant stars.
DOUBLE CLUSTER — the great double cluster in Perseus glows cold and dense through the dome slit, two rich knots of blue-white stars blazing in the black.
CRESCENT MOON LOW — a cold crescent moon sets through a thin strip of cloud visible in the dome slit, a solitary star trembling bright beside it.
PERSEIDS OVERHEAD — multiple perseid meteors cross the cold black sky above the open terrace simultaneously, brief white scratches burning fast across the dense star-field.
CLOUD RIFT STARS — a long cold rift tears through storm cloud above the terrace, exposing a brilliant corridor of stars and one steady bright planet beyond.
FULL MOON IN THE DOME — a great full moon hangs perfectly centred in the dome opening, its cratered face brilliant white against the black, cold light flooding the brass instrument below.
MILKY WAY THROUGH THE SLIT — the dense river of the galaxy crosses the dome gap, ten thousand cold stars packed into that pale band against absolute black.
METEOR ACROSS THE GAP — a bright meteor streaks hard and fast through the dome slit, leaving a brief luminous scratch across the cold black field of fixed stars.
ECLIPSE CORONA ABOVE THE DOME — the dark disc of the total eclipse hangs in the open sky, its white corona flaring in ragged petals against the cold surrounding black.
